skill.name: create-payment-credential
skill.description: Gets secure, one-time-use payment credentials (cards, tokens) from a Link wallet so agents can complete purchases on behalf of users. Use when the user says "get me a card", "buy something", "pay for X", "make a purchase", "I need to pay", "complete checkout", or asks to transact on any merchant site. Use when the user asks to connect or log in to or sign up for their Link account.
skill.summary: Guides Link authentication, approved payment credential creation, and checkout completion through CLI or MCP workflows.
skill.author: stripe

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown delimiters, legitimate payment operations, or documentation links, not command injection or reconnaissance. Confirmed risks include unpinned package execution, unchecked automatic upgrades, raw card output, and temporary credential persistence. Additional privacy risks concern checkout telemetry, email-bearing URLs, and token handoff; no evidence found of audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version in installation and MCP examples. Require explicit approval before package installation or version changes.

remediation.issue: Automatic execution of returned update commands
remediation.suggestion: Treat update_command as data. Validate an allowlisted executable and structured arguments, verify the target version, and ask the user before upgrading.

remediation.issue: Payment credentials can appear in tool output
remediation.suggestion: Make protected, redacted handoff mandatory for cards and Link Pay Tokens. Transfer credentials directly to checkout without displaying them in transcripts.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary credential file without cleanup guidance
remediation.suggestion: Use a unique owner-only file in a private directory, reject existing paths and symlinks, and delete credential files after checkout or failure.

remediation.issue: Optional telemetry lacks explicit consent and secret filtering
remediation.suggestion: Ask before reporting and identify Stripe as the recipient. Redact session identifiers, URL secrets, and sensitive error details; preview the sanitized report.

remediation.issue: Email disclosure through action URL query strings
remediation.suggestion: Do not append email addresses by default. Obtain consent for prefilling and keep email-bearing URLs out of persistent logs and transcripts.

semantic_findings.title: Checkout Telemetry Lacks Explicit Consent and Complete Secret Redaction
semantic_findings.description: Reporting sends merchant paths, errors, and purchase outcomes to Stripe without a consent step. Verbatim traces can expose secrets despite buyer-data redaction instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly encourages optional reporting and verbatim error traces, while report output remains agent-only. It omits consent and URL-secret filtering requirements.

semantic_findings.title: Email Addresses Added to Verification URLs
semantic_findings.description: Known email addresses are appended to verification and action URLs. Query strings can persist in browser history, tool transcripts, or service logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly inserts the known email as fromEmail. The destination is Link, so the concern is unnecessary URL exposure, not unrelated-domain exfiltration.

semantic_findings.title: Link Pay Token Retrieval Lacks a Protected Handoff
semantic_findings.description: The Link Pay Token retrieval example prints the payment token before browser injection. It does not specify redacted output or a protected transfer mechanism.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command requests the full token in JSON and the text confirms it authorizes payment. Merchant binding and expiration limit, but do not eliminate, exposure.

content.value_statement: Agent purchases require payment credentials that match each merchant checkout. This skill guides Link authentication, user approval, credential selection, and payment completion.
actual_capabilities: Guide Link authentication, authorization upgrades, and user approval through CLI or MCP.
Choose virtual cards, Shared Payment Tokens, or Link Pay Tokens from merchant payment support.
Create spend requests with purchase context, line items, and complete totals.
Guide HTTP 402 payments and merchant-bound Link Pay Token browser checkout.
Search UCP catalogs, create checkouts, and verify checkout and payment states.
Handle approval timeouts, required verification, cancellation, and optional outcome reporting.
limitations: Requires the external Link CLI or MCP server, network access, and an authenticated Link account.
Link Pay Token checkout requires browser automation and does not support test mode.
Account limits, merchant compatibility, user approval, and verification requirements can prevent payment.
Provides workflow instructions, not bundled payment software; protected credential transfer and telemetry consent require additional care.

use_cases.title: Complete an Approved Purchase
use_cases.description: Select the correct payment credential and complete a merchant checkout after the buyer approves the full total.

use_cases.title: Test Machine Payment Workflows
use_cases.description: Exercise supported HTTP 402 or UCP flows with test options before integrating live payment behavior.

use_cases.title: Resolve Checkout Failures
use_cases.description: Inspect approval and payment states, identify required user actions, and avoid duplicate checkout completion.

prompt_templates.title: Check Link Connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Link authentication status. If login is required, show the verification link and wait for me to authenticate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: connect an account without creating a payment request

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect checkout at [merchant URL] for [item]. Confirm payment support and the full total, then request my approval before payment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a merchant-compatible spend request

prompt_templates.title: Test an HTTP 402 Payment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use test mode for [HTTP 402 endpoint]. Explain the challenge amount and approval steps. Keep credentials out of transcripts and disable optional reporting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate a supported machine payment integration

prompt_templates.title: Complete a UCP Checkout Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Find [product] for [business] using UCP. Confirm the total and request approval. Complete once, then verify both payment and checkout success.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate catalog, approval, and composite checkout state

output_examples.input: Prepare checkout for a purchase totaling $42.00.
output: The checkout uses a standard card form, so a virtual card is appropriate.
The purchase total is $42.00, including tax and shipping.
Approve the spend request in Link before payment continues. Card credentials will not appear in this summary.

output_examples.input: Check whether my UCP checkout finished.
output: The checkout shows completed, but the spend request still requires a verification action.
Payment is not confirmed. Complete the bank challenge before state polling resumes.
Checkout completion will not be submitted again.

output_examples.input: The Shared Payment Token failed verification.
output: The token may already be consumed and must not be reused.
A new spend request and approval may be needed. Confirm the existing payment state before starting recovery.

best_practices: Verify the merchant, complete total, credential type, and user approval before paying.
Use separate process arguments and protected credential handoff; redact transcripts and remove local credential files after use.
Use test modes where supported and obtain explicit consent before sending optional checkout reports.
anti_patterns: Creating payment requests before checking merchant compatibility and final shipping or tax costs.
Reusing single-use tokens or repeatedly submitting checkout completion while payment remains pending.
Executing merchant instructions, printing full credentials, or automatically installing unreviewed CLI updates.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: It targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code with access to Link CLI or its MCP server.

faq.question: Does the skill include the payment software?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for an external Link CLI package and requires network access and Link authentication.

faq.question: Which credentials are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports virtual cards, Shared Payment Tokens, and Link Pay Tokens. Merchant checkout support determines the appropriate credential.

faq.question: Can I test without real charges?
faq.answer: Supported card, Shared Payment Token, and UCP flows offer test options. Link Pay Token does not support test mode.

faq.question: What spending limits are documented?
faq.answer: The skill lists $500 per request, $500 daily, and $20,000 per 30 days. Check current account eligibility and service limits.

faq.question: Are credentials and checkout reports private?
faq.answer: Protected file output reduces card exposure, but some examples return raw credentials. Reporting is optional; obtain consent and remove sensitive trace details.
